findings.description: Static AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the instance user_data script. User data is stored unencrypted and is readable by any local process via the instance metadata service (http://169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) and by any principal with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, so these long-lived IAM credentials are trivially exfiltrated.

No metadata_options block is set, so the instance defaults to allowing IMDSv1 (http_tokens = "optional"). Any SSRF or command-injection flaw in the Apache service exposed on port 80 can read instance metadata and user data — which in this configuration contains hard-coded AWS credentials — without a signed token.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block specifies encrypted = true, so the instance root volume is created unencrypted unless account-level EBS default encryption happens to be enabled. Data at rest, including the user-data-derived credentials cached on disk, is unprotected.

The instance is launched into aws_subnet.web_subnet, which sets map_public_ip_on_launch = true and routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, so it receives a public IP and is directly reachable from the internet. There is no bastion, load balancer, or NAT boundary in front of it, and the public DNS name is exported as an output.

Ingress rule opens TCP port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration on a publicly-addressed instance to the entire internet. This permits credential brute-forcing and immediate exploitation of any SSH daemon vulnerability, and is the primary path to the hard-coded credentials in user data.

Ingress allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 and no HTTPS listener or TLS termination exists anywhere in the configuration, so all traffic to and from the web host traverses the internet unencrypted and is subject to interception and modification.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. On a compromised host this places no constraint on outbound command-and-control channels or bulk data exfiltration, removing a key defence-in-depth control.

The EBS volume attached to the web host omits encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), leaving the volume and its underlying snapshots unencrypted at rest with no KMS key protection.

The snapshot is taken from the unencrypted aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage and therefore inherits its unencrypted state. Snapshots are independently shareable and copyable artefacts, so an unencrypted snapshot broadens the exposure of the volume's data beyond the original instance.

The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so network flow records — which reveal internal topology, addressing, and communication patterns useful to an attacker — are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, so it relies entirely on account-level defaults to prevent public ACLs or policies from being applied later. Sensitive network telemetry could become publicly readable through a single subsequent ACL or policy change.
There is no bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so flow log objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.

force_destroy = true is set on the audit log destination bucket with no versioning, object lock, or MFA delete. Network flow evidence can be irrecoverably deleted along with the bucket, undermining the integrity of the only network-level audit trail in this configuration.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway means every instance launched here is automatically internet-facing. This is an insecure default that removes network segmentation and silently exposes any future workload placed in the subnet.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the public route table (aws_route_table.web_rtb, which routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway) make this subnet public by default, so any instance placed in it is directly reachable from the internet without explicit opt-in.
